report.currency: EUR (company reports in euro; tables in € millions unless stated, with ~USD equivalents at EUR/USD 1.105)
report.verdict: A clean, margin-rich quarter — revenue +10.0% to €8.72m (~$9.63m), EBIT +79.6% to €3.04m (~$3.36m) at a 34.9% margin, net profit more than doubled — that the market ignored because the same release announced a second re-cut of the B2B platform deal from 1 Nov 2026: lower fees, affiliate/royalty costs pushed to partners, and a €5.25m (~$5.8m) one-off "incentive" to be settled by forgiving partner receivables in exchange for five-year contracts. The P&L is strong; the thesis now lives in the cash line (9M operating cash flow €2.2m against €7.5m net profit) and in a €21.6m receivable book that is 82% of total assets. Shares fell ~26% intraday.
summary: **Headline beat on every P&L line, but no consensus to beat.** Q3-26 revenue rose 9.96% YoY to €8,717,367 (~$9.63m), EBIT +79.6% to €3,044,040 (~$3.36m), EBIT margin 34.92% (Q3-25: 21.38%), net profit +114.8% to €2,628,384 (~$2.90m), EPS €0.0351 (~$0.039) vs €0.0163. Figures cross-check to the IAS 34 condensed statements (ISRE 2410-reviewed), the Cision/Inderes release and Finwire/Privata Affärer coverage. Sequentially revenue was +3.2% vs Q2-26 (€8.45m) and EBIT +6.3% (€2.86m). The only published sell-side numbers (Carlsquare, Aug-26) implied ~€9.9m/€2.3m for Q4, not Q3; there is no Q3 consensus.

**9M-26 shows the full effect of the January-2025 B2B cost shift.** Revenue +12.0% to €25.48m (~$28.15m), gross margin 56.1% (44.1%), opex −4.1%, EBIT +103.7% to €8.82m (~$9.75m) at 34.6% (19.0%), net profit +147.5% to €7.54m (~$8.33m), EPS €0.1005 (~$0.111) vs €0.0406. FY-25 as a whole delivered €30.56m revenue / €6.48m EBIT, so 9M-26 EBIT already exceeds all of FY-25.

**The quarter decelerated hard after mid-August — management did not say so, the maths does.** The Q2 trading update put average daily NGR through 18 Aug at +21.08% vs the whole of Q3-25; the quarter closed with net game win +12.0% and revenue +10.0%. Back-solving (our estimate), the final ~43 days ran roughly +2% YoY on net game win and about −3% on revenue — i.e. growth stalled from late August. PremierGaming's 'higher customer winnings' explains only ~€0.2m of that.

**Margin structure: gross margin 55.3% (+835bps YoY), opex 20.4% of revenue (−520bps).** Direct costs (payment processing, affiliate, licence/software fees, gaming taxes) fell 7.4% YoY to €3.89m (~$4.30m) on revenue +10%; marketing −24% to €0.25m (2.8% of revenue), personnel −8% to €0.80m, other external −16% to €0.70m. Derived EBITDA (EBIT + D&A, not a company metric) €3.08m (~$3.40m), 35.3% margin.

**Below the line is odd for a debt-free company.** 'Finance expenses' of €414k (~$0.46m; 4.8% of revenue; 9M €1.28m) are described as mainly FX-rate effects, not interest. Tax was €1.4k on €2.63m PBT — Starfish Media N.V. (Curaçao) treats its profits as foreign-sourced and untaxed, and the Maltese entities report no chargeable income. A ~0% effective tax rate is a structural feature and a structural risk.

**Platform KPIs: volume up, monetisation down.** Customer deposits +25.4% YoY to €26.03m (~$28.8m); gross game win +8.3% to €12.29m; net game win +12.0% to €11.87m (~$13.1m); 'hold' (NGW/deposits) 45.6% vs 51.0% (−540bps YoY, −90bps QoQ). Active customers 27,783 (−1.7% YoY, +2.4% QoQ); new registrations +59% to 25,971 but new depositing customers −2.9% to 7,662 — registration-to-deposit conversion collapsed to 29.5% from 48.3%. NGW per active rose to €427 (~$472) from €375; bonus cost (GGW−NGW) fell to 3.4% of GGW from 6.6%.

**B2C (PremierGaming, Malta/Sweden) shrank to 1.11% of revenue from 3.48% in Q2** — roughly €0.10m (~$0.11m) vs €0.29m, our derivation — on 'higher customer winnings'. Management pivoted it to a niche product strategy: Prontolive.se moved to the latest platform build, a 5-year Swedish gaming-software licence (28 Aug 2026–27 Aug 2031) was obtained, the ProntoChoice slot and the 'Volameter' volatility search tool launched, and marketing was stepped up in Q4. October new unique depositing players were +103% MoM; LTV is unproven.

**Marlin Media (marvn.ai / marvnBoost) remains a cost centre with no disclosed revenue.** marvnBoost moved to three subscription tiers plus a free trial and exhibited at SBC Summit Lisbon; the group is now repositioning it toward custom content pipelines for aggregators/providers under a new brand, and has added headcount. marvn.ai organic search traffic came under pressure as search engines cut referrals to independent publishers. The Q2 report extended Marlin's break-even target to end-2026 — Q4 will tell.

**The real news: a second B2B model reset from 1 Nov 2026.** Angler will confine its B2B offer to the proprietary iGaming platform and discontinue non-software B2B services. Under an agreement in principle (formal contracts not yet executed), partner fees fall ('lower revenues'), while affiliate and royalty costs tied to partners' operations move to the partners, and Angler's 'exposure to certain operational and commercial risks' is reduced. Management expects 'significant changes to the Group's revenue and cost structure' and says profitability 'may' be significantly affected during a transition period.

**A €5.25m (~$5.8m) one-off 'commercial incentive' will be settled by writing down partner receivables.** It is conditional on partners signing new five-year contracts and 'would be effected through a corresponding reduction in existing amounts receivable'. That equals 24% of the €21.6m receivable book, 26% of group equity and 70% of 9M-26 net profit. IFRS treatment is 'being assessed' — an immediate P&L charge (credit-loss/consideration payable to a customer) versus a contract asset amortised against revenue over five years is the swing factor for Q4 and FY-26 reported earnings.

**No guidance, by design.** Angler has never given numeric guidance; it now states the financial impact of the new arrangements 'cannot currently be estimated with sufficient reliability'. The CEO's letter is explicit that revenue and profit will fall from 1 Nov while arguing the streamlined software model builds 'a strong foundation for future growth and improved profitability'. Carlsquare's August FY-26 estimates (revenue €35.4m / EBIT €11.1m) are stale.

**Cash conversion is the weak link.** 9M-26 operating cash flow €2.20m (~$2.43m) versus net profit €7.54m — 29% conversion — because debtors absorbed €7.42m. Trade and other receivables reached €21.60m (~$23.9m), +€3.1m QoQ and +52% since December, equal to 82% of total assets and ~230 days of 9M revenue. Note 18 discloses a €3.5m (~$3.9m) 'business development' facility to a B2B client that stopped accruing interest after Q1-25 and is repayable only out of that client's revenue share; no impairment is recognised.

**Balance sheet is debt-free but asset-light and receivable-heavy.** Cash €3.24m (~$3.58m; Jun-26 €2.59m, Dec-25 €1.24m), no borrowings, equity €20.32m (~$22.5m; 77% equity ratio), trade/other payables €6.07m. 9M capex €0.20m (intangible additions €0.20m); derived 9M FCF €2.00m (~$2.2m). Net cash/EBITDA is not meaningful; the relevant leverage is to partner credit quality.

**Capital returns are on hold.** No FY-25 dividend was recommended and no interim is declared (FY-24 paid €0.0133/share, €997k, in June 2025). A 2023 option scheme covers up to 2.88m shares (3.7%) with extended vesting; share count unchanged at 74,984,995, so basic = diluted EPS.

**Organisation: technology is being ring-fenced in Aegirsoft Ltd.** Software development is being consolidated into Aegirsoft (incorporated 12 Jan 2026), to be completed in 2026, with Nicholas Formosa (ex-head of the B2B platform for seven years) appointed its CEO. This is the entity that will carry the 'software-only' B2B proposition; Starfish Media N.V. (Curaçao) still books 'a significant portion' of group revenue.

**Share price: the market priced the reset, not the quarter.** The stock fell ~26% to SEK 4.29 by 09:21 CET on 12 Nov (prior close ~SEK 5.80 implied, Inderes data) and by 16 Nov was ~SEK 3.55 (market cap ~SEK 266m), roughly −39% since the release; Inderes shows a trailing P/E of ~5.4x. The official 12-Nov close could not be verified.

**Thesis read-through: earnings quality, not earnings level, is the debate.** Bulls get a 35%-margin, debt-free platform business with five-year partner lock-in and lower operational risk at ~5x trailing earnings. Bears note that 2025-26 profits were largely booked as receivables, that a quarter of those receivables is now being forgiven to keep the partners, that the partners evidently hold the negotiating leverage, and that the growth engine stalled in September before the fee cut even began.

**Disclosure quality is thin for a company making a structural pivot.** One reportable segment (IFRS 8), partners unnamed, no B2B/B2C revenue split beyond a percentage, no quantification of the fee reset, KPI definitions quietly changed in Q3 ('sites utilising the Group's proprietary iGaming platform' vs 'sites supported by the Group'), and 'available cashflow from operations' used to describe the cash balance. The next hard data point is the Q4/FY-26 report on 18 Feb 2027.

segments.name: B2B iGaming platform (Starfish Media N.V. / Aegirsoft Ltd) — c.99% of group revenue
segments.headline: Record platform quarter on deposits +25% and a 55% gross margin, but monetisation slipped, growth stalled from late August, and the fee structure is being cut from 1 Nov in exchange for five-year contracts and a €5.25m receivable write-down.
narrative: Angler reports a single IFRS 8 segment, so the B2B platform business has to be read through the group KPIs net of the B2C share management discloses. On that basis B2B and other revenue was about €8.62m (~$9.53m) in Q3-26, up roughly 5.8% on the €8.15m implied for Q2 and the engine of the group's +10% YoY print; management attributes it to 'strong momentum' from prioritising the proprietary, partner-configurable platform over the past two years. Volume was the story: customer deposits across partner sites rose 25.4% YoY to €26.03m (~$28.8m) and 10.7% QoQ, gross game win rose 8.3% to €12.29m (~$13.6m) and net game win 12.0% to €11.87m (~$13.1m). The gap between deposit growth and win growth is the first thing to notice — 'hold', which Angler defines as net game win over deposits rather than win over wagers, fell to 45.6% from 51.0% a year ago and 46.5% in Q2, so roughly thirteen points of the deposit growth leaked out through player withdrawals or wins. Revenue captured 73.4% of net game win versus 77.2% in Q2 and 74.8% in Q3-25; management does not explain the ratio, but with B2C negligible it is effectively the blended platform/fee take, and it moved the wrong way before the fee cut even started.

Customer economics were mixed and the funnel deteriorated. Period-unique actives were 27,783, down 1.7% YoY though up 2.4% QoQ; new registrations jumped 59% to 25,971 (flat on Q2), yet new depositing customers slipped 2.9% to 7,662, so registration-to-deposit conversion fell to 29.5% from 48.3% a year earlier — consistent with cheaper, lower-intent traffic being pushed into partner sites. Monetisation per head improved: net game win per active was €427 (~$472) against €375, deposits per active €937 (~$1,035) against €735, and bonus cost (gross less net game win) fell to 3.4% of GGW from 6.6%, the cleanest sign that partners, not Angler, are now carrying promotional spend. Over nine months the picture is harsher on counts — cumulative actives 56,106 (−20%) and new depositors 20,882 (−22%) — offset by deposits +18% and NGW +10%. We would also flag that the active-customer definition was narrowed in Q3 to sites 'utilising the Group's proprietary iGaming platform' from sites 'supported by the Group', which may flatter the QoQ comparison at the margin.

Cost structure is where the January-2025 renegotiation still shows. Direct costs — payment processing, affiliate fees, product and software licence fees and gaming taxes — were €3.89m (~$4.30m), 44.7% of revenue versus 53.0% in Q3-25, so gross margin reached 55.3% (+835bps YoY, +25bps QoQ) and 56.1% for the nine months. Marketing was €0.25m (~$0.27m), just 2.8% of revenue (Q3-25: 4.1%), personnel €0.80m (−8%) and other external €0.70m (−16%); total opex of €1.78m (~$1.97m) is 20.4% of revenue, down 520bps. The result is an EBIT margin of 34.9% on a cost base that is essentially fixed at ~€1.8m a quarter, which is why incremental revenue has dropped through at close to the gross margin for three quarters. The flip side is that the same operating leverage works in reverse when the fee base is cut.

The intra-quarter trajectory deserves more attention than management gave it. The 20 August trading update stated that average daily net gaming revenue through 18 August was 21.08% above the Q3-25 full-quarter average; the quarter then closed with net game win +12.0% and revenue +10.0%. On our arithmetic (an estimate, since the update's 'net gaming revenue' is not precisely defined), the remaining 43 days ran at roughly +2% YoY on net game win and about −3% on revenue — i.e. growth effectively stopped from late August. PremierGaming's adverse customer-winnings swing accounts for only ~€0.2m of the shortfall, so the platform partners themselves slowed. Carlsquare's August note had taken the trading update as confirmation that 'the revenue inflection ... is now firmly established'; the exit rate says otherwise.

The structural event is the second B2B re-cut, effective 1 November 2026 under an agreement in principle (formal five-year contracts not yet executed, expected 'in the near term'). Angler will provide only its proprietary iGaming platform and discontinue 'non-software-related B2B services'; partners will pay under a 'revised fee structure, resulting in lower revenues', while affiliate and royalty costs associated with partners' operations transfer to the partners and the group's 'exposure to certain operational and commercial risks' falls. To secure the deals Angler has agreed in principle a one-off €5.25m (~$5.8m) 'commercial incentive', conditional on the five-year signatures and 'effected through a corresponding reduction in existing amounts receivable from the B2B partners'. Read plainly: the partners owe Angler money, are not being asked to pay a quarter of it, and in return commit to a cheaper platform fee for five years. That is a reasonable commercial trade for a vendor whose counterparties hold the leverage, but it is also an admission that 2025-26 accrued revenue was partly uncollectable at face value. The IFRS treatment is unresolved — an immediate charge (expected-credit-loss or consideration payable to a customer) versus a contract asset amortised against revenue over five years decides whether Q4-26 prints a loss.

The receivable book is the balance-sheet expression of the same issue. Trade and other receivables were €21.60m (~$23.9m) at 30 September, up €3.1m QoQ and €7.4m since December, equal to 82% of total assets and ~230 days of nine-month revenue; nine-month operating cash flow was €2.20m against €7.54m of net profit, a 29% conversion. Note 18 adds a €3.5m (~$3.9m) 'business development support' facility advanced to a B2B client for a casino project on the Starfish platform — interest ceased after Q1-25, Angler is released from further funding, repayment is 'contractually linked to the B2B client's share of revenues', and management sees no impairment indicator. Note 7 states that 'a significant portion' of group revenue comes from the Curaçao subsidiary and that performance is 'materially dependent' on that entity's continued success and regulatory compliance. Concentration, credit and counterparty leverage are therefore the same risk wearing three hats.

Segment guidance is qualitative only. The CEO expects 'a reduction in the revenues and profits due to the new B2B business model as from 1st of November 2026', and the board states the overall impact 'cannot currently be estimated with sufficient reliability'; no partner names, fee rates or cost-transfer amounts are given. Our working assumption (estimate, wide range) is that platform revenue under the new model runs 25-45% below the Q3 run-rate with direct costs falling proportionately more, leaving the EBIT margin broadly intact but the EBIT base 20-35% lower once the transition settles — before any one-off charge. The technology consolidation into Aegirsoft Ltd under Nicholas Formosa, due to complete in 2026, is the organisational counterpart of the 'software-only' pitch; it does not change the economics.

segments.name: B2C — PremierGaming Ltd (Malta/Sweden licences, Northern Europe)
segments.headline: Down to 1.11% of group revenue on adverse customer winnings; the niche re-launch (Swedish software licence, ProntoChoice, Volameter) doubled October depositors but lifetime value is unproven and the unit is immaterial to group earnings.
narrative: PremierGaming, the group's only regulated B2C operator, represented 1.11% of Q3-26 revenue — about €0.10m (~$0.11m) on our derivation — down from 3.48% (≈€0.29m) in Q2-26, with management citing 'higher customer winnings in Q3'. That is a swing of roughly €0.2m QoQ, or ~2% of group revenue, and it is the only luck-driven element in the quarter the company identifies. Angler does not disclose B2C actives, deposits, ARPU or marketing separately, so the unit cannot be benchmarked against Swedish peers on hold or cost per acquisition.

The quarter was spent re-tooling. Prontolive.se was migrated to the latest version of the group's B2B platform software; the Swedish Gambling Authority granted PremierGaming a licence to supply gaming software for online gaming, valid 28 August 2026 to 27 August 2031; the first in-house slot, ProntoChoice, was launched under that licence (development outsourced 'for efficiency'); and the 'Volameter', a search tool letting players filter slots by volatility, went live at the very end of September. The stated logic is differentiation for recreational players under the company's own Swedish brands rather than scale.

Post-quarter, marketing was increased for the Swedish brands and new unique depositing players in October rose 103% versus September. Management is careful to say the next step is to 'follow up the lifetime value and plan accordingly', and the Q2 report had committed to repeating campaigns only where lifetime value by margin exceeds campaign cost. A doubling from a base that produced ~€0.1m of quarterly revenue is encouraging but not yet material; what matters is whether Q4 B2C revenue recovers toward the 3-7% of group it represented in 2025 without eroding the group's 2.8%-of-revenue marketing ratio.

No segment guidance is given. The strategic value of PremierGaming is less its P&L than its role as the in-house reference customer for the platform and as the group's only exposure to a fully regulated, taxed market — the counterweight to a revenue base that is otherwise concentrated in a Curaçao-registered subsidiary.

segments.name: Marlin Media Ltd — marvn.ai / marvnBoost (affiliate & AI content, B2B)
segments.headline: Commercial model defined (three tiers, free trial) and a pivot toward content pipelines for aggregators and game providers, but no revenue disclosed, organic traffic under pressure and a break-even target of end-2026 that looks stretched.
narrative: Marlin Media closed the quarter with marvnBoost, its proprietary AI content engine for iGaming teams, 'moving from launch to a defined commercial model': three subscription tiers are on the market and a free trial was introduced to shorten the path to first use. The product debuted at SBC Summit Lisbon (29 Sep–1 Oct), which management says generated strong direct feedback from providers, operators and affiliates and 'validated the commercial positioning'. First paying customers had been secured in Q2-26; neither customer numbers nor revenue are disclosed, and nothing in the group P&L suggests the contribution is material.

Two shifts are worth noting. First, demand at the show 'pointed consistently beyond the platform's current content scope', so Marlin is now building custom content pipelines for game aggregators, service providers and game providers — a segment management describes as needing content at scale and underserved by agency models — and will rebrand to reflect the wider remit, adding headcount to do so. Second, marvn.ai's organic visibility 'came under pressure' as generic search engines reduced traffic to independent publishers; management frames this as confirming a repositioning of marvn.ai from a search-traffic asset to a product with an engaged user base, with multilanguage support and data enrichment in development. The affiliate-SEO channel that was the original Marlin thesis is, in other words, being de-emphasised.

Financially the unit is a cost centre inside a group whose opex is only ~€1.8m a quarter. The Q2 report extended Marlin's break-even objective to end-2026; with headcount being added and the core traffic engine weakening, that target looks ambitious. The relevant balance-sheet line is intangible software of €1.50m (~$1.66m) after €0.20m of 9M additions and €77k amortisation; management concluded there were no impairment indicators at period end. No segment guidance is given beyond consolidating around a B2B revenue model led by marvnBoost.

Our view: Marlin is optionality, not valuation support. It matters to the equity story only if marvnBoost converts the Lisbon pipeline into recurring contracts before the group's platform fee cut compresses the cash available to fund it.

highlights.text: EBIT margin 34.9% (+1,354bps YoY, +101bps QoQ) on gross margin 55.3% and opex at 20.4% of revenue — the January-2025 shift of payment/operating costs to partners is fully embedded and the cost base is flat at ~€1.8m (~$2.0m) a quarter.
Platform volumes at record levels: deposits +25.4% YoY to €26.0m (~$28.8m), net game win +12.0% to €11.9m (~$13.1m), NGW per active +14% to €427 (~$472); bonus cost down to 3.4% of GGW from 6.6%.
Debt-free balance sheet: cash €3.24m (~$3.58m), up from €1.24m at December with no financing inflow; equity €20.3m (~$22.5m), 77% equity ratio; derived 9M FCF €2.0m (~$2.2m), +117% YoY.

Five-year partner contracts under the new model would lock in the platform relationship and move affiliate/royalty costs and 'certain operational and commercial risks' to partners — a lower-revenue but lower-risk, more software-like profile if executed.
PremierGaming's niche re-launch produced +103% MoM new depositing players in October, backed by a 5-year Swedish gaming-software licence (to Aug-2031), the ProntoChoice slot and the Volameter tool.
Net profit +114.8% to €2.63m (~$2.90m) and 9M EPS €0.1005 (~$0.111) already 56% above FY-25's €0.0643; trailing P/E ~5.4x after the sell-off (Inderes).

lowlights.text: Second B2B fee reset from 1 Nov 2026: management explicitly expects lower revenue and profit, cannot estimate the impact, and the formal five-year agreements were still unsigned at publication — the entire earnings base is being repriced with no numbers.

€5.25m (~$5.8m) one-off 'incentive' settled by forgiving partner receivables = 24% of the €21.6m book, 26% of equity and 70% of 9M net profit; IFRS treatment undecided, so Q4 could print a loss of ~€3m if expensed (our estimate).

Cash conversion 29%: 9M operating cash flow €2.20m (~$2.43m) vs net profit €7.54m; receivables €21.6m (~$23.9m) are 82% of assets and ~230 days of revenue, plus a €3.5m interest-free facility to a B2B client repayable only from its revenue share.

Growth stalled inside the quarter: +21.1% daily NGR through 18 Aug became +12.0% NGW / +10.0% revenue for the full quarter, implying roughly flat-to-negative YoY for the last six weeks (our arithmetic) — before the fee cut.
Hold 45.6% (−540bps YoY), actives −1.7%, new depositors −2.9% and registration-to-deposit conversion down to 29.5% from 48.3% — volume growth is coming from more deposits per head, not more heads.

B2C PremierGaming fell to 1.11% of revenue from 3.48% on adverse customer winnings; Marlin Media still has no disclosed revenue, is adding headcount, and its marvn.ai traffic engine is being hit by search-engine referral declines.

Governance/disclosure: one reportable segment, unnamed partners, revenue 'materially dependent' on a Curaçao subsidiary with a ~0% effective tax rate, FX-driven 'finance expenses' of €0.41m (4.8% of revenue) with no debt, and a quietly narrowed active-customer definition.

forecast.intro: Angler does not issue numeric guidance, so the 'bridge' is from implicit expectations to an explicit warning. Before Q3 the only published framework was Carlsquare's August model (FY-26 revenue €35.4m / EBIT €11.1m, implying ~€9.9m / €2.3m for Q4) built on the +21% trading update. The Q3 release replaces that with a qualitative statement from the B2B division — effectively the whole company — that revenue and profit will fall from 1 November 2026 under a revised fee structure, partly offset by affiliate/royalty costs transferring to partners, with 'significant' transition-period effects on profitability and a €5.25m (~$5.8m) incentive whose accounting is unresolved. B2C and Marlin are immaterial to the bridge.

forecast.view:
**Q4-26 (our estimate, wide range):** October runs on the old model at roughly the Q3 pace (~€2.9m revenue, ~€1.0m EBIT); November–December run on the new fee structure. Assuming platform revenue 25–45% below the Q3 run-rate and direct costs falling from 45% of revenue toward ~30–35% as affiliate and royalty costs transfer, we model Q4 revenue of **€6.1–7.3m (~$6.7–8.1m)** and EBIT of **€1.9–2.6m (~$2.1–2.9m)**, i.e. an EBIT margin still in the low-to-mid 30s but an absolute EBIT 15–35% below Q3 — before any one-off. FY-26E therefore lands at **revenue ~€31.6–32.8m (~$35–36m)** versus Carlsquare's €35.4m, and **EBIT ~€10.7–11.4m (~$11.8–12.6m)** pre-charge, close to the old street number only because Q3 over-delivered. If the €5.25m is taken through the P&L in Q4 (credit-loss or consideration-payable-to-customer treatment), FY-26 EBIT drops to roughly **€5.5–6.2m** and Q4 prints a loss; if it is capitalised as a contract asset, the drag is ~€1.05m a year against revenue from 2027. We lean toward an immediate charge being the more conservative reading of 'reduction in existing amounts receivable', but the company has not decided.

**FY-27 is where the reset bites fully.** A full year at the new run-rate implies revenue of roughly **€21–26m (~$23–29m)** against ~€32m in FY-26E, and EBIT of **€7–9m (~$8–10m)** if the margin holds in the 33–36% band — a 20–35% earnings reset that the ~39% share-price fall has broadly discounted at ~5x trailing earnings. The margin assumption is the key risk: management's own language ('may have a significant impact on profitability during a transition period') suggests costs do not fall in lock-step with fees in the first quarters.

**Leverage direction: none to speak of, but cash is the tell.** With no debt, the balance-sheet question is whether the €16.3m of receivables remaining after the incentive actually convert to cash under the new contracts. If partners pay down even half of that over 2027, cash would multiply from €3.2m and a dividend could return; if receivables keep growing faster than revenue, the 'incentive' was the first write-down, not the last. We would also expect FX-driven finance expenses (~€0.4m a quarter) and the ~0% tax rate to persist, so net profit should track EBIT less ~€1.5m a year.

**Swing factors:** (1) the fee rate and cost-transfer mechanics in the final contracts; (2) IFRS treatment and timing of the €5.25m; (3) hold normalising back toward 50% (worth ~€1m of quarterly NGW at current deposit levels); (4) whether the September stall was seasonal or partner-specific; (5) PremierGaming cohort LTV versus the stepped-up Q4 marketing.
watch: Execution of the definitive five-year B2B agreements and disclosure of the fee structure, plus the stated IFRS treatment of the €5.25m incentive (P&L charge vs contract asset) — likely in the Q4/FY-26 report on 18 Feb 2027.
Q4-26 revenue and direct-cost ratio for November–December (first two months under the new model) and any January–February 2027 trading update; we model a 25–45% revenue step-down vs the Q3 run-rate.
Receivables: does the €21.6m book (net €16.3m after the incentive) shrink and convert to cash; recoverability of the €3.5m B2B client facility; any further expected-credit-loss provisions.
Platform KPIs: hold recovery from 45.6% toward the ~50% of 2025, new-depositing-customer trend after −2.9% YoY, and whether registration-to-deposit conversion recovers from 29.5%.
PremierGaming: Q4 share of revenue versus 1.11% in Q3, lifetime value of the October cohort, and marketing as % of revenue versus the 2.8% group ratio.
Marlin Media: evidence of recurring marvnBoost revenue against the end-2026 break-even target, and impairment testing of the €1.5m software intangible at year-end.
Capital allocation: dividend resumption for FY-26 (Carlsquare had pencilled in 2027) versus the need to fund transition-period cash flow; option-scheme vesting.
Regulatory/tax: continued ~0% effective tax under the Curaçao territorial stance and the 'material dependence' on the Curaçao subsidiary; any change in partner licensing jurisdictions.
